newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen rebounding to 15,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen rebounding to 15,000 level.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to recover on Wednesday, recouping Tuesday's losses in line with Wall Street's upturn, but brokers said caution ahead of the local market's long holiday would limit upside.

"I would not be surprised to see the index bounce 200 points or more today," said Peter Lui, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities. "But we are likely to see profit-taking around the 15,000 level."
The Hang Seng Index closed 130.27 points lower at 14,890.96 on Tuesday, shaken by the Dow's 192-point drop on Monday and worries about the U.S. dollar.
But the Dow Industrials recovered overnight, rising 153.80 points to 7,758.06. The Hang Seng London Reference Index gained 98.79 points to 14,989.75.

"There is likely to be a good bit of volatility today, ahead of the expiration of the (June) futures," said a broker at BZW Securities Asia. "Then I think volatility will drop off in advance of the long holiday."
The June futures contract expires on Thursday.
The market will be closed from June 28 through July 2, with normal trading to resume on July 3.
